articles.description: Prime minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said the country could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with the US president, Donald Trump, failed to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. articles.title: Tejas Mk1A By March 2027? Air Chief Sets Deadline As IAF Battles Fighter Squadron Shortage | News18
articles.description: A major update for India's indigenous fighter aircraft programme! Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit says the first squadron of the Tejas Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Mark 1A is expected to join the IAF within the current financial year, by March 2027. Speaking at the ANI National Security Summit 3.0 in New Delhi, Dixit says four key areas identified for improvement in the aircraft have been addressed in collaboration with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), bringing the programme closer to induction. articles.title: Apple Music's Drake helped steer the unfilmable 'Neuromancer' to Apple TV
articles.description: Rapper Drake's production company is one of those behind the first-ever TV dramatization of William Gibson's said to be unfilmable "Neuromancer" novel, which debuts on Apple TV in January 2027. Callum Turner in "Neuromancer" - image credit: Apple TV Apple TV already has a reputation for high-budget science fiction series such as "For All Mankind" and "Silo." But because of "Foundation," it also has a reputation for attempting to make series out of science fiction that's previously been considered unfilmable. That's the case again with "Neuromancer," which Apple TV greenlit back in February 2024. Now the producers behind the dramatization of William Gibson's famous novel say that Apple Music's Drake has been key to the production, and to it coming to Apple TV. articles.title: SpaceX Successfully Catches Starship Spacecraft With Giant Launch Tower Arms For First Time
articles.description: SpaceX achieved a major milestone in its Starship programme as the spacecraft's upper stage returned from orbit and was caught by giant mechanical 'chopstick' arms at the company's Starbase facility in Texas. Starship completed a 22-and-a-half-hour orbital flight, circling Earth 14 times and deploying 26 Starlink satellites before its historic recovery. The mission marked the first successful tower catch of a Starship upper stage, although the Super Heavy booster experienced a navigation problem during its return and later exploded over the Gulf of Mexico.
